source.title: From Dormant to Deleted: Tamper-Resistant Unlearning Through Weight-Space Regularization
source.authors: Shoaib Ahmed Siddiqui; Adrian Weller; David Krueger; G. Dziugaite; M. Mozer; Eleni Triantafillou

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: It directly tests whether fine-tuning can restore performance after unlearning, with retraining from scratch as a reference, but does so for example-level unlearning in vision classifiers rather than LLM knowledge unlearning.
record.gate_note: The study tests fine-tuning-based recovery and quantization in vision classifiers. It does not test activation-direction ablation or recovery through prompt changes, languages, jailbreaks, or in-context information. LLM findings about fine-tuning and quantization in the text are cited background, not this study's results. Many figure comparisons are described qualitatively without exact values in the text.
record.test_reason: The study measures its own results on whether fine-tuning or quantization restores unlearned information after approximate unlearning, with a retrain-from-scratch reference. It also tests whether tamper-resistance methods hold up. The setting is new: example-level unlearning in ResNet vision classifiers, not LLM knowledge unlearning. That makes it T3 rather than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors add four points: forget-set influence stays dormant, recoverable from the retain set alone; resistance is predicted by weight-space distance from the pretrained model; TAR fails in their setting; and their vision models do not show quantization-based recovery. They acknowledge a trade-off between tamper-resistance and test accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates example-level unlearning in vision classifiers rather than the cited LLM unlearning methods. Its relearning attack fine-tunes on the retain set, sometimes with a subset of forget examples; it also tests weight-space interventions and quantization.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome varies with the unlearning method, typicality of forgotten examples, subclass versus class-agnostic setting, dataset, model size, unlearning budget, and choice of fine-tuning examples. Weight Dist Reg becomes susceptible on ResNet-34 when ResNet-18 hyperparameters are transferred; retain-set examples induce more recovery than unseen test examples, especially with zero or few forget examples.

fits_no_version.finding: Vulnerable unlearned models stay close to the pretrained model in L2 distance and stay linearly mode-connected to it. Retrain and the robust methods sit behind a loss barrier. L2 distance predicts tamper-resistance better than LMC (Figs 4–5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Susceptibility to relearning is predicted by small weight-space distance and linear mode connectivity between the unlearned and original models (influence stays dormant rather than deleted).

fits_no_version.finding: A simple loss-threshold MIA gives near-chance accuracy for methods that are vulnerable to relearning (e.g. SCRUB 51.6%, Circuit Breakers 55.0%) (Table 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Standard privacy or forgetting metrics can miss residual, recoverable influence of the forget set.

record.problems: The experiments use small vision classifiers and example-level forgetting, which is not the same as removing LLM knowledge or capabilities. Many headline comparisons are figure-only or described qualitatively without exact values or uncertainty estimates. The authors also report sensitivity to model size and hyperparameter transfer.
record.rows_left_out: Individual figure-only comparisons for additional baseline methods and settings in Figures 2, 9–13 were not transcribed separately where the text reports only an aggregate or qualitative comparison; the paper's explicit results about typical and random forget sets are discussed as cases where the retrain-from-scratch model already predicts nearly perfectly.

untested.parts: LLM knowledge unlearning and general language ability. Utility here is only image test accuracy.
LLM fact or knowledge relearning. Truly unrelated relearning data is not tested; the retain set and test images come from the same distribution.
No activation-direction ablation. Weight-space L2 and LMC analysis is suggestive but does not show blocked access.
No prompting, rephrasing, jailbreak, language or in-context tests.
Resistance to non-fine-tuning attacks other than quantization; LLM settings.

missing.what: TAR fails to add tamper-resistance beyond the initial safeguard
Class-agnostic atypical forget set: many methods reach ~100% after relearning while retrain stays very low
CIFAR-100 results; CBFT shows significant resistance there
ResNet-34: Weight Dist Reg becomes susceptible with transferred hyperparameters (the text also contradictorily calls it highly robust)
Unlearning-budget dependence. After 0-example relearning, Catastrophic Forgetting is 99.99% at 1 epoch and 66.14% at 100. Weight Distortion is 61.07% at 1 epoch and 58.59% at 100.
Trade-off: the most tamper-resistant methods have the lowest test accuracy

record.verdict_notes: Several corrections to the record. Its version ids V1/V2/V4/V6 map to A/B/D/F. The tranche changes from T2 to T3 because the setting is vision example-level unlearning. Reader errors fixed: the 'A supports' label based on the retrain control is dropped. Baseline rows r10, r16 and r19 are set to none. On Imagenette, SCRUB and Weight Dist Reg never reached the retrain reference after unlearning. Two internal inconsistencies remain: the Fig 6 caption versus the main text, and App. E on Weight Dist Reg. All verdicts concern ResNet classifiers, not LLMs.

versions.untested_parts: The experiments concern example-level unlearning in vision classifiers, not whether LLM unlearning preserves general language-model ability.
Tests retain-set fine-tuning and relearning with subsets of the forget set; does not test LLM knowledge recovery or specifically characterize all unrelated or loosely related examples.
No activation-direction ablation or experiment showing that an unlearning method blocks access rather than deletes knowledge.
Tests quantization on vision models, not low-bit quantization of LLM weights.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery tests.
Tests the paper's proposed methods in vision classifiers; does not establish resistance to the full range of attacks in LLMs.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 atypical sub-class forget set (SCRUB, Circuit Breakers, Random Relabeling); Imagenette SCRUB
relationships.reason: After unlearning to near the retrain level, retain-only fine-tuning lifts forget accuracy to near 100% (r1–r3). On Imagenette, SCRUB never reached the reference (85.71% vs 67.53%) and rose to 93–94% (r13–r15).
relationships.display_finding: Forget accuracy recovered to nearly 100% on CIFAR-10, while Imagenette SCRUB rose from 85.71% to 93–94% against a retraining reference of 67.53%.

source_check.notes: Table 1 is column-scrambled but reads as Unlearned / 0 Relearn / 10 Relearn blocks. The text says Imagenette retrain stays 'close to 50%', but the table gives 63-67%; the Imagenette architecture is not stated. The Fig 6 quantization result is readable only down to about 8 bits, where models collapse. Relearning fine-tunes on the full retain set plus 0-100 forget examples.

statements.correction: SCRUB, CIFAR-10 ResNet-18, atypical forget set (App G, Fig 13): fine-tuning on test or JPEG-corrupted test examples instead of the retain set recovers forget accuracy a bit less, mostly at 0 or few forget examples. The gaps shrink as forget examples increase. No numbers are given.
statements.problem: The cited r8 sits under 'modest or no recovery' from loosely related text, in a challenges group. The study says unseen same-distribution examples make relearning only 'a bit less pronounced'. That qualifies B (l2 limits_scope); it does not challenge it.
The Fig 6 caption wording conflicts with the main text. Below about 8 bits the model collapses, so lower bit widths can't be read.

statements.correction: Weight Dist Reg on Imagenette: forget acc 84.42% after unlearning (retrain 67.53%). After retain-set relearning: 73.87% with 0 forget examples, 75.77% with 10 (retrain 63.53% / 64.16%). The text calls it the exception. Main support is CIFAR-10 ResNet-18: Weight Distortion and Weight Dist Reg are 'significantly more tamper-resistant' (Fig 2; r5, r6), with no numbers.
statements.problem: The statement cites r20 but says nothing about this study.

statements.correction: TAR as a second phase on CIFAR-10 (Fig 3 text, no row): no added tamper-resistance. In the same figure, CBFT and Weight Dist Reg as a second phase substantially improve resistance. Weight Distortion and Weight Dist Reg are significantly more tamper-resistant on CIFAR-10 (Fig 2). Weight Distortion on Imagenette: 74.03% to 78.86% (0) and 81.09% (10), vs retrain 63.53% / 64.16% (r17, r18).
statements.problem: The TAR sentence is right. The cited rows r17 and r18 are Weight Distortion on Imagenette, which shows partial resistance (F limits_scope, l5), not TAR. The opening claim that resistance methods in vision slow relearning little or not at all does not fit this study's own methods.
